title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 sketchbook geolocation audit
scope: Backend-only spatial calibration of selected filmed sketchbook pages against correspondence, historical maps, landmark geometry and landscape form.
frontend_policy: Do not expose this image-derived layer or any sketchbook image on public Pages in this phase.

method.principle: Represent the precision actually supported by the evidence. Do not convert field areas, travel corridors or inferred sightlines into false exact points.
method.modern_coordinate_guard: Modern coordinates are used only as geometric control points. They do not by themselves prove a nineteenth-century viewpoint.
method.image_reading_guard: A place/date identification inferred by synchronizing an image with correspondence must not be described as an inscription unless the graphite itself supports that reading.

baseline.label: Maricopa railroad settlement/station vicinity
baseline.coordinate_status: approximate modeling baseline, not a surveyed 1892 viewpoint

terrain_candidates.name: Sierra Estrella / Hayes Peak sector
terrain_candidates.reason: Long rugged range rising beyond a broad desert plain is compatible with the sketch. Sierra Estrella runs on a NW-SE alignment and is the dominant high range northwest of the Maricopa baseline.

terrain_candidates.name: Table Top Mountains sector
terrain_candidates.reason: A comparable-distance southern mountain candidate; retained because the sketch alone does not yet determine viewing direction.

historical_controls.title: Map of Maricopa County Arizona Showing Salt River Valley ...
historical_controls.institution: Arizona State Library, Archives and Public Records / Arizona Memory Project
historical_controls.use: period railroads, roads, relief/hachures, desert land and county-scale context

historical_controls.title: Sierra Estrella Peak / Hayes Peak modern terrain control
historical_controls.use: control coordinate and range identity only; not historical evidence

current_result.recommended_geometry: field-area ellipse/polygon around Maricopa desert, with candidate sightline NW to Sierra Estrella stored only as hypothesis

cases.delta_from_pass1: Sierra Estrella confidence raised slightly because independent range geometry confirms a prominent NW-SE range at the correct distance/bearing; no exact viewpoint claim.

cases.inscription_status: high-confidence visual reading after contrast review
cases.assessment: Same-day Maricopa landscape group. The caption can be upgraded from medium-high to high confidence. Mountain identification remains open; Sierra Estrella is currently the leading candidate, not a secure identification.
cases.recommended_geometry: same Maricopa field-area object as p04-p05, but preserve page-level distinction

reasoning: The sketch follows the securely dated Maricopa group in the filmed sequence.

Rudolf's San Diego retrospective account explicitly describes a rocky range behind chaparral and cactus across Arizona to Yuma, then a widening near-barren California desert, the below-sea-level Salton depression, and finally a climb past snow-covered San Jacinto.
The sketch shows a large steep rocky massif rising abruptly from sparse stony desert. This is compatible with a San Jacinto/Colorado Desert view but is not diagnostic enough for a point.

historical_controls.use: same-year Southern Pacific route control for California, Arizona and the Sunset route

historical_controls.title: Amerine & Wilson's indexed township & county map of California
historical_controls.use: same-year California rail/topographic context; eastern San Bernardino and San Diego counties shown separately

current_result.recommended_geometry: rail corridor segment only; no marker

cases.guard: Do not assign a point or named peak until silhouette/rail-mile evidence improves.

cases.visible_note: Yucca brevifolia [probable visual reading; not yet a diplomatic transcription]
cases.identification_basis: correspondence + distinctive ecology + landscape morphology, not an inscription
cases.archive_control: Agua Caliente letter of 7 May retrospectively describing Hesperia on 5 May

historical_controls.title: Map No. 1 of Hesperia San Bernardino County, Cal.; showing town and acre properties
historical_controls.use: recover early townsite and railroad relation

historical_controls.title: Hesperia
historical_controls.date: circa 1890; catalogue says Hesperia was laid out in 1891
historical_controls.use: second townsite-map control; later than map no.1 according to Huntington

historical_controls.title: Hesperia Train Station historical marker
historical_controls.use: locational proxy only: marker says the 15 x 20 ft moveable station stood directly across Hesperia Road; California Southern used Hesperia as a stopping point

historical_controls.title: Hesperia Hotel historical marker
historical_controls.use: locational proxy only: records the three-story hotel at the same marker area from 1887; useful because Rudolf says he stayed at a hotel near the station

proxy_model.coordinate_status: modern historical-marker location; the marker text places the original station directly across Hesperia Road, so this is a proxy, not an exact 1892 building coordinate
proxy_model.assessment: Both high-peak controls cluster in a narrow southeast sector. The sketch cannot distinguish the peaks. The proper inference is a broad southeast view toward the San Bernardino high country.

current_result.recommended_geometry: field area around historic hotel/depot townsite plus broad SE view sector; backend route-revision candidate for 5 May

cases.correction_from_pass1: Withdraw the earlier claim that the graphite itself reads 'Wüste bei Hesperia' or carries a 5 May date. Close image inspection instead suggests the botanical phrase Yucca brevifolia.

historical_controls.title: Admiralty Chart No. 453 Port Antonio Jamaica

view_model.hypothesis: shipboard point offshore north of Port Antonio, looking generally south into/along the harbour entrance
view_model.example_point_status: illustrative geometry only, not a claimed historical position
view_model.assessment: The left/right landmark order is robust for an offshore northern approach. The visibly banded lighthouse strengthens the Folly Point identification; distance offshore remains unresolved.

current_result.recommended_geometry: broad offshore approach/departure corridor or view sector north of the harbour, never an exact point

cases.assessment: Both are laid-in tropical water/palm drawings and visually belong to the same material group as p23. Port Antonio is plausible after the p23 landmark match, but neither page has a diagnostic landmark yet.

current_result.recommended_geometry: unmapped candidate association until shoreline/building topology can be matched

cases.external_control: A Bremen local-history source independently attests Chr. Baldewein & Sohn at Am Wall; Schüsselkorb is a historic central Bremen street.
cases.assessment: These notes make Bremen more than a terminal label: the sketchbook also functioned as a travel logistics/address notebook. Date and purpose are unresolved, so no new itinerary point is created.

cases.transcription: Von New York bis Bremen sind 880 geographische Meilen
cases.interpretation: A travel-distance calculation for the Atlantic passage. 880 geographical miles is about 6,530 km, plausibly a rounded route-distance estimate rather than a geometric straight-line measurement.
cases.journey_relation: Strongly associated with the New York–Bremen return/transatlantic sequence; no independent date appears on the page.

research_conclusions: The filmed sketchbook, as presently observable, begins with securely legible Maricopa material dated 24 April rather than a visible Tempe 22 April page; preserve the catalogue-surrogate conflict.
Page 17 remains a strong Hesperia match, but because of correspondence and ecological synchrony rather than a place/date inscription. The visible note is probably Yucca brevifolia.

Pages 26-27 demonstrate that the object functioned as a working travel notebook as well as a landscape sketchbook: addresses/logistics and a New York-Bremen distance calculation sit alongside field views.
Maricopa, Hesperia and Port Antonio can be represented at finer spatial scales than city markers, but only in the backend and with explicit geometry classes and confidence.
Page 23 remains the strongest landmark-based geolocation candidate; Folly Point is strengthened by the matching banded lighthouse morphology and its 1888 construction date.
Page 12/13 remains a corridor hypothesis; same-year Southern Pacific mapping supports the route reconstruction but does not identify the mountain.
next_work: Maricopa: construct candidate horizon profiles or angular ridge envelopes toward Sierra Estrella and Table Top from plausible 1892 station/desert positions; compare ridge ordering to pages 5 and 9.
Hesperia: obtain the highest-resolution Huntington townsite map, georeference railway, hotel and road geometry, and use the HMDB marker only as a secondary control.
Port Antonio: use harbour chart topology to draw a backend-only view-sector polygon and test whether p21/p25 are compatible with adjacent ship positions.
California corridor: use the January 1892 Southern Pacific timetable map to constrain the train path through Yuma-Salton-Indio and test p12/13 against major massifs without forcing a point.
Bremen notes: check a circa-1892 Bremen address directory for Baldewein & Sohn, Schüsselkorb 14 and the unresolved Zimmermann line.
Keep all resulting image references and spatial hypotheses in research/backend only.
